newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves West Bank settlement expansion.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves West Bank settlement expansion.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai has approved a plan to build many more homes in a Jewish settlement in the West Bank, drawing fire on Wednesday from Palestinians and Israeli peace activists.

"No doubt this decision which has been taken by Mr. Mordechai concerning building new houses is another breaching of what has been agreed upon and what has been signed," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in Gaza.
News of the decision came only hours before Mordechai and Arafat were due to meet for the first time in an attempt to restart implementation of Palestinian self-rule in Gaza and the West Bank.

Pinhas Wallerstein, head of the Council of Jewish Settlers, said the 1,800 housing units would be built in Matityahu, a settlement for ultra-orthodox Jews near the pre-1967 Middle East war border between Israel and the West Bank.
A Defence Ministry spokeswoman declined to confirm the 1,800 unit figure.

"This is the largest approval to build since the government was formed and overturned the freeze on settlement building," Peace Now spokesman Alon Arnon told Reuters, estimating the new units would lead to a fourfold increase in Matityahu's current population of about 2,400.

"This is surprising and worrying that before the Mordechai-Arafat meeting permission is given for such a large expansion of settlements...and raises questions as to the government's intentions," he said.
U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross, in Gaza for talks with Arafat, called settlements a problem.

"The American policy on settlement activity has not changed. We continue to see it as a problem. We continue to see it as the kind of activity that complicates the negotiating process," Ross told reporters.
Mordechai's moves were in line with the decision by the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to nullify the previous Labour administration's freeze on most settlement building.
"I am glad the defence minister finally approved it," Wallerstein told Army Radio. "I understand that once all the planning stages are completed, the investor can start building."

Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. Some 130,000 Jews have settled amidst the nearly two million Palestinians in the territories since Israel captured them in the 1967 Middle East war.
